Consult Summary:
- Acute gastrointestinal symptoms with 3 days of diarrhoea, central abdominal pain, and vomiting; no blood in stool and no definite fever; patient remains able to talk and ambulate.
- Likely gastroenteritis; plan is supportive care with hydration, avoid antibiotics, and in-person GP follow-up if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute gastroenteritis (diarrhoea for ~3 days with abdominal pain and vomiting) with associated symptoms.
  - Timeline/progression: Onset ~3 days ago; diarrhoea persists; abdominal pain present centrally; vomiting occurred this morning; currently eating small amounts but stools/urination frequent; no blood in stool; no definite fever; patient reports needing to go to toilet frequently (near-continuous urge).
  - Systems review: GI – diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting; no haematochezia or melaena reported. Respiratory – past asthma; no shortness of breath reported. General – able to walk/talk; no chest pain.
  - Exam findings: Abdominal tenderness when pressed; pain localized to central abdomen; patient able to eat/drink some; no fever noted in history; no explicit vitals provided.
  - Medications: Asthma inhaler (brand/dose/frequency not documented); patient mentions using a new inhaler.
  - Allergies: NKDA.
  - Social history: Has asthma; paternal history of bowel cancer (father died ~10 years ago); no other social history details provided.
  - Differential/durther inputs: Gastroenteritis suspected; infection-related diarrhoea vs foodborne illness discussed.

Issue 2:
- Dehydration risk due to reduced oral intake with diarrhoea and vomiting.
  - Timeline: Reports inadequate water intake; ongoing vomiting and diarrhoea.
  - Associated factors: Frequent toilet visits; not drinking enough fluids.
  - Plan/management: Emphasize drinking lots of water and fluids; monitor for fever or worsening symptoms; stay home until mildly better.
  - Exam/Objective data: No explicit dehydration signs documented; not provided vitals.

Issue 3:
- Anxiety about family history of bowel cancer; concern for possible GI cancer.
  - Timeline: Father died of bowel cancer about 10 years ago.
  - Patient concern: Worries about cancer given family history.
  - Clinician assessment: Symptoms more suggestive of gastroenteritis; less likely that this represents familial bowel cancer; if symptoms worsen, GP in person can evaluate abdominal exam.
  - Plan: Reassure; advise GP visit in real life if worsening or persistent.

Medications:
- Asthma inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); new inhaler brand mentioned.

Allergies:
- NKDA (no known drug allergies).

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.

Social History:
- Not documented beyond asthma and family history; patient expresses concern about father's bowel cancer.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- General: Patient alert and able to converse; vitals not provided.
- Abdominal: Central abdominal pain with palpation tenderness; no explicit guarding or rebound described.
- Respiratory/Cardiovascular: History of asthma; no chest pain or dyspnea reported at this visit.
- Other: No blood observed in vomit per patient; no GI bleeding reported.

Plan:
- Advise gastroenteritis management: drink lots of water/fluids; monitor for fever or worsening symptoms.
- Avoid antibiotics as they are not helpful in this scenario.
- Stay home while symptoms persist or improve gradually; return to work when tolerating times between toilet visits improve.
- If symptoms worsen or do not improve, book an in-person GP visit to assess abdomen.
- If fever develops or red flags occur, seek urgent care or GP evaluation.

Follow-up:
- Patient to book a GP appointment if symptoms worsen or persist; consider in-person evaluation after a couple of days.

Quality checks:

- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (BP, HR, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation) not documented.
  - Full medication reconciliation beyond asthma inhaler (no dose/route/frequency) and no complete list of current meds.
  - Preventive health history (immunizations, screening tests) not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Date of birth/conflicting age details: patient corrected year during intake; initial date given (1992) conflicted with later statements about age. Conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some repetition, filler words, and minor confusion (birth year correction) → overall usable but indicates noisy intake.
